delta_summary.moral_floor: The moral floor cracked in multiple places this week — judicial process, press independence, voting-rights enforcement, and truthful public communication — though it did not give way completely, held in part by scattered court rulings, career-official dissent, and one governor's public restraint.
delta_summary.net_interpretation: The week's near-stillness on the clock should not be read as equilibrium; it reflects a system absorbing simultaneous shocks from military deployment, judicial retreat, and the rapid weaponization of a political assassination, with resilience present but reactive rather than preventive.

traits_moved.note: Twenty-four traits registered measurable movement this week, with all but one deteriorating; the sole improvement reflected continued judicial pushback in the Carroll defamation case.

long_synopsis: This week the Democracy Clock barely moved, but stillness masked saturation, not calm. Federal forces surged into Chicago, Baltimore, Boston, Washington, and Memphis under war-styled rhetoric, while the Supreme Court's shadow docket permitted racial profiling and let Trump remove an independent FTC commissioner without full briefing. An 8th Circuit ruling gutted private enforcement of the Voting Rights Act as multiple states pressed parallel challenges. Then Charlie Kirk was assassinated at Utah Valley University, and within days the tragedy became a weapon against ordinary political speech, with firings, blacklist proposals, and false accusations spreading before facts emerged. FBI Director Kash Patel's chaotic handling of the case deepened doubts about law-enforcement competence. Courts, career officials, and one governor's public restraint offered scattered resistance, but the floor cracked in more places this week than in almost any before it.
short_synopsis: Federal deployments against cities, a Supreme Court profiling ruling, coordinated retreat from voting-rights enforcement, and an assassination converted into a tool against dissent combined to strain democratic norms on nearly every front, even as scattered judicial and civic resistance held.
